specAnchors.text: understand why entropy changes occur during: i changes of state ii dissolving of a solid ionic lattice iii reactions in which there is a change in the number of moles from reactants to products

primer.text: Entropy rises when matter or energy becomes more dispersed. Melting and boiling increase it sharply, condensing and freezing lower it; forming a gas in a reaction raises it; dissolving a solid trades lattice order for aqueous mobility. This note reads entropy signs from state symbols and works the classic endothermic examples where disorder still increases.

modules.title: Entropy and changes of state
modules.opening: State changes are entropy's clearest signature. Melting unlocks a lattice into mobile liquid, boiling scatters particles into gas, and the reverse changes lock order back in. The entropy sign follows the state ladder: solid below liquid below gas.
keyPoints: Whenever a substance changes state, its entropy shifts too.
Entropy increases on melting: the regular lattice becomes an irregular, mobile arrangement of particles that rotate and slide.
Entropy increases significantly on boiling, since gas particles move freely and sit far apart.
Entropy decreases on condensing and on freezing, as particles are drawn into more regular arrangements.
Raising a substance's temperature raises its entropy at every stage, as particles become more disordered.

low.restatement: Melting and boiling raise entropy, condensing and freezing lower it; the ladder runs solid, liquid, gas upward.
low.analogy: A library: books shelved (solid), stacked loosely on tables (liquid), and flung across the room (gas).
low.examPointer: Read the state symbols of any equation - the ladder gives the entropy sign instantly.

medium.restatement: Order costs nothing to lose and much to keep; each step up the state ladder trades positional information for freedom, which is the entropy gain.
medium.analogy: A marching band breaking formation: individuals gain freedom with every step from column to crowd.
medium.examPointer: Boiling earns the word 'significantly' - the gas step dwarfs the melting step.

modules.title: Gases made and solids dissolved
modules.opening: Two everyday changes carry reliable entropy signs. Making a gas from condensed phases raises entropy sharply, as in calcium carbonate's thermal decomposition. Dissolving a solid trades lattice order for aqueous mobility - usually a gain, though the water around each ion loses some freedom, so the balance is not automatic.
keyPoints: Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate produces carbon dioxide gas, so the system's entropy increases.
The carbon dioxide molecule is far more disordered than the solid reactant, moving constantly.
Ethanoic acid with ammonium carbonate also forms a gas while dropping slightly in temperature, an endothermic change whose disorder still rises as solution and gas form.
Dissolving ammonium nitrate in water is endothermic (delta H = +25.7 kJ mol^-1), with disorder rising as fixed lattice ions become free to move.
For ionic solids generally, breaking lattice bonds raises disorder while making solvent bonds lowers it, so the sign is not always predictable.

low.restatement: Gas from solid or liquid: entropy up. Dissolving: lattice order lost, some water order gained - usually a net gain, sometimes not.
low.analogy: Letting birds out of a cage fills the room (gas), while making friends with the neighbours (hydration) tidies their corner a little.
low.examPointer: For dissolving, name both effects - lattice breaking and hydration ordering - before predicting.

medium.restatement: The gas step dominates because a gas multiplies positional options enormously; dissolution mixes a loss of lattice order with a gain in ionic mobility, and the ledger can land either way.
medium.analogy: Empting a wardrobe into a wardrobe-sized suitcase: most clothes gain freedom, but some must be folded tight (hydration shells).
medium.examPointer: Quote the ammonium nitrate example with its +25.7 kJ mol^-1 when illustrating endothermic dissolution.

modules.title: Two solids that go cold
modules.opening: Barium hydroxide with ammonium chloride is the lecture-theatre classic: two ordered solids form a paste, the temperature plunges, and ammonia gas escapes. Entropy wins because the products leave the low-entropy solid state for liquid water and gaseous ammonia.
keyPoints: Mixing barium hydroxide with ammonium chloride forms a paste and the temperature drops significantly, marking an endothermic process.
The reaction forms barium chloride solution, gaseous ammonia and water from two solids.
The ammonia gas is detected by smell and turns damp red litmus paper blue.
Two solids alone have very low entropy, so a liquid or gas product raises the entropy strongly.
The entropy change depends on the physical states of the products, not just on the energy changes.

low.restatement: Two low-entropy solids yield liquid and gas: the temperature drop signals endothermy, while the state jump up the ladder pays for it.
low.analogy: Paying for a house move with the freedom of a bigger city: costly on the day, liberating afterwards.
low.examPointer: The litmus test for ammonia - damp red paper turning blue - is the standard detection line.

medium.restatement: Solids hoard order; anything that escapes into gas or liquid cashes that order in. The cold paste is enthalpy's bill, and the gas is entropy's receipt.
medium.analogy: Breaking a safe open: expensive effort (heat drawn in) rewards you with contents scattered freely (gas).
medium.examPointer: Answer template: endothermic yet feasible because delta S is strongly positive.

glossary.definition: A melting, boiling, condensing or freezing change, each with a characteristic entropy direction.
The regular arrangement of particles in an ionic or atomic solid, whose order keeps entropy low.
The loss of freedom suffered by water molecules as they arrange around dissolved ions.

figures.caption: The entropy of a substance increases when the temperature is raised as particles become more disordered
